stages.name: Deserts & oases
stages.desc: Desert, oases and mining lands beyond the settled Nile valley

stages.name: Egyptian kings
stages.desc: The 13th Dynasty, then the native kings of Thebes

stages.name: Levantine settlers
stages.desc: Canaanite communities and the 14th Dynasty kings of Avaris

states.name: North Sinai
timeline: The Ways of Horus, the coastal road across Sinai to Canaan
The Hyksos control the road between Avaris and Canaan
Ahmose's army marches across Sinai after the retreating Hyksos
The road to Canaan is in Egyptian hands

states.name: Aswan
timeline: Elephantine and the Lower Nubian forts are held by Egyptian garrisons
Kush takes the Nubian forts; Buhen's garrison now serves the ruler of Kush
A Kushite army with its allies raids north as far as Elkab
Kamose campaigns in Lower Nubia and restores Egyptian rule at Buhen
Ahmose campaigns south against Kush

states.name: Red Sea
timeline: Eastern Desert of the Medjay, nomads who serve Thebes as scouts and archers

states.name: Matrouh
timeline: Western Desert and coast, home to Libyan herders

states.name: New Valley
timeline: The Kharga and Dakhla oases, linked to the Nile by desert tracks
Desert roads link the Hyksos and Kush, bypassing Thebes

states.name: Suez
timeline: Desert between the Delta and the Gulf of Suez

states.name: South Sinai
timeline: Turquoise mines of Serabit el-Khadim, worked with Canaanite labour

states.name: Port Said
timeline: Lagoons and harbours of the Pelusiac Nile, settled from the Levant
The Hyksos control the Delta's eastern harbours
The eastern harbours pass to Ahmose

states.name: Dakahlia
timeline: Eastern Delta towns under the 14th Dynasty of Avaris
Under the Hyksos kings
Fighting spreads through the eastern Delta
Returned to Egyptian rule with the fall of Avaris

states.name: Al Sharqia
timeline: Avaris, a harbour town of Canaanite settlers, is the seat of the 14th Dynasty
Avaris becomes the capital of the Hyksos kings and grows to some 250 hectares
Kamose's fleet threatens Avaris, but the city holds
Ahmose's army and fleet besiege Avaris
Avaris falls and is plundered; the Hyksos withdraw to Canaan

states.name: Ismailia
timeline: Levantine villages in the Wadi Tumilat, such as Tell el-Maskhuta
Tjaru, the frontier fortress on the Ways of Horus, is held by the Hyksos
Ahmose's army breaks into Tjaru, cutting Avaris off from Canaan

states.name: Damietta
timeline: Northeastern Delta under the 14th Dynasty of Avaris
Under the Hyksos kings
Returned to Egyptian rule with the fall of Avaris

states.name: Kafr el-Sheikh
timeline: Central Delta, nominally under the failing 13th Dynasty
Under the Hyksos kings
Returned to Egyptian rule with the fall of Avaris

states.name: Beheira
timeline: Western Delta, nominally under the 13th Dynasty
Under Hyksos overlordship
Returned to Egyptian rule with the fall of Avaris

states.name: Alexandria
timeline: Western Delta coast, nominally under the 13th Dynasty
Under Hyksos overlordship
Returned to Egyptian rule with the fall of Avaris

states.name: Cairo
timeline: Heliopolis, city of the sun god, under the 13th Dynasty
Heliopolis passes to the Hyksos
Ahmose's army enters Heliopolis

states.name: Giza
timeline: Memphis, Egypt's ancient capital, under the 13th Dynasty
Memphis falls to the Hyksos; the 13th Dynasty collapses
Kamose's troops raid the Bahariya oasis road, part of this governorate
Ahmose's army fights its way toward Memphis
Memphis returns to Egyptian rule

states.name: Minya
timeline: Hermopolis and Beni Hasan under the 13th Dynasty
Hermopolis and Nefrusy are held by vassals of the Hyksos
Kamose sacks Nefrusy, the stronghold of the Hyksos vassal Teti
Middle Egypt returns to Theban rule

states.name: Faiyum
timeline: The Faiyum, near the royal residence of Itjtawy
Itjtawy is abandoned; the Faiyum falls under the Hyksos
Retaken by Ahmose

states.name: Beni Suef
timeline: Nile valley south of Itjtawy, under the 13th Dynasty
Under the Hyksos kings
Kamose's war reaches the region
Retaken by Ahmose

states.name: Monufia
timeline: Southern Delta farmland under the 13th Dynasty
Under the Hyksos kings
Returned to Egyptian rule with the fall of Avaris

states.name: Qalyubia
timeline: The Delta's southern apex under the 13th Dynasty
The Hyksos raise the great earthen enclosure of Tell el-Yahudiya
Taken by Ahmose's army on its way to Avaris

states.name: Gharbia
timeline: Central Delta, nominally under the failing 13th Dynasty
Under the Hyksos kings
Returned to Egyptian rule with the fall of Avaris

states.name: Sohag
timeline: Abydos, holy city of Osiris, under the 13th Dynasty
Abydos under the Theban kings
Ahmose builds his pyramid and temples at Abydos

states.name: Qena
timeline: Coptos and Dendera under the 13th Dynasty
Under the Theban kings
Seqenenre builds a fortified palace at Deir el-Ballas

states.name: Asyut
timeline: Asyut and Cusae under the 13th Dynasty
Cusae, at the governorate's northern edge, marks the frontier with the Hyksos
Kamose launches his war from the frontier at Cusae
Theban control is pushed north of Cusae

states.name: Luxor
timeline: Thebes, a provincial city of the 13th Dynasty
Thebes becomes a royal capital as the north falls to the Hyksos
King Seqenenre Tao is killed; Kamose, his successor, takes up the war
Ahmose becomes king; his mother Ahhotep holds Thebes

events.title: Itjtawy's waning court
events.text: Short-lived kings of the 13th Dynasty rule from Itjtawy, near Lisht, as royal power fades.

events.title: Avaris of the Asiatics
events.text: At Tell el-Dab'a, a harbour town of Canaanite settlers, soldiers, sailors and traders has grown for generations.

events.title: King Nehesy
events.text: The 14th Dynasty, kings with Canaanite as well as Egyptian names, rules the eastern Delta from Avaris.

events.title: Byblos and Egypt
events.text: Byblos, the Canaanite port of cedar, keeps its old trade and its kings' Egyptian-style titles.

events.title: Hazor at its height
events.text: Hazor in northern Canaan is one of the largest cities of the Middle Bronze Age Levant.

events.title: Famine and plague
events.text: Bietak's excavations find hasty mass graves at Avaris, signs of an epidemic in the late 14th Dynasty.

events.title: Heqa khasut
events.text: A new line of kings, the Hyksos 15th Dynasty, takes power at Avaris under the title 'ruler of foreign lands'.

events.title: Memphis falls
events.text: The Hyksos take Memphis; the 13th Dynasty collapses and its court abandons Itjtawy.

events.title: Kush takes the forts
events.text: Kerma's kings take over Egypt's fortresses at the Second Cataract.

events.title: Thebes alone
events.text: A line of Theban kings rules Upper Egypt, from Elephantine to the Hyksos frontier at Cusae.

events.title: Serving Kush
events.text: At Buhen, an Egyptian named Ka records on his stela that he served the ruler of Kush.

events.title: Tell el-Yahudiya
events.text: A vast earthen enclosure rises north of Heliopolis, a Hyksos stronghold or camp.

events.title: Kerma at its height
events.text: Kerma, capital of Kush, builds great temples and royal tumuli with hundreds of sacrificed retainers.

events.title: Ways of Horus
events.text: Tjaru guards the coastal road across Sinai linking Avaris to the cities of Canaan.

events.title: King Khyan
events.text: Khyan, the most powerful Hyksos king, sends gifts abroad; a lid bearing his name was found at Knossos on Crete.

events.title: Khyan at Gebelein
events.text: A block bearing Khyan's name south of Thebes hints at Hyksos reach deep into Upper Egypt.

events.title: Severed hands
events.text: Pits before the throne room of the Hyksos palace at Avaris hold the right hands of slain enemies, trophies of war.

events.title: Tell el-Ajjul
events.text: A rich Canaanite city near Gaza, likely ancient Sharuhen, trades gold and goods with Avaris.

events.title: Horses on the Nile
events.text: Horses, a novelty from the Levant, are buried at Avaris; the chariot will follow.

events.title: Statues to Kerma
events.text: Egyptian statues taken in Nubian raids are set up as trophies in Kerma's tombs.

events.title: Raid on Elkab
events.text: An inscription in the tomb of Sobeknakht at Elkab tells of a great invasion by Kush and its allies, beaten back.

events.title: King Apepi
events.text: Apepi begins a reign of about forty years at Avaris, the longest of the Hyksos kings.

events.title: Trade across the frontier
events.text: Thebes and Avaris trade in cattle and grain; Theban herds graze in the Delta by agreement.

events.title: Medjay archers
events.text: Nomadic Medjay of the Eastern Desert serve Thebes as scouts and archers.

events.title: Rhind papyrus
events.text: A scribe in Apepi's thirty-third year copies the Rhind Mathematical Papyrus, a treasure of Egyptian learning.

events.title: Deir el-Ballas
events.text: Seqenenre Tao builds a fortified palace and camp north of Thebes, a base for war.

events.title: The hippopotamus quarrel
events.text: A later tale says Apepi complained that the Theban hippopotami kept him awake, a pretext for war.

events.title: Seqenenre killed
events.text: Seqenenre dies of axe, dagger and spear wounds to the head, possibly executed after capture in battle.

events.title: Kamose marches north
events.text: Kamose overrules his cautious council and sails north to fight the Hyksos.

events.title: Nefrusy sacked
events.text: Kamose destroys the stronghold of Teti, a Hyksos vassal in Middle Egypt.

events.title: The intercepted letter
events.text: On the oasis road Kamose captures Apepi's messenger, carrying a plea to the ruler of Kush to attack Thebes.

events.title: Kamose at Buhen
events.text: Kamose campaigns in Lower Nubia, retaking Buhen from Kush.

events.title: Kamose's stelae
events.text: Kamose sets up stelae at Karnak boasting of his war; he reached Avaris but could not take it.

events.title: Ahmose, boy king
events.text: Kamose dies; the young Ahmose, Seqenenre's son, becomes king, with his mother Ahhotep as regent.

events.title: Queen Ahhotep
events.text: A stela at Karnak praises Ahhotep for rallying the soldiers and pacifying Upper Egypt.

events.title: Ahmose goes north
events.text: Ahmose leads the army and fleet down the Nile into Hyksos territory.

events.title: Heliopolis and Tjaru
events.text: Notes on the Rhind papyrus record Heliopolis entered and Tjaru taken, cutting Avaris off from Canaan.

events.title: Avaris falls
events.text: After repeated battles, Avaris is taken and plundered; the Hyksos are driven out toward Canaan.

events.title: Siege of Sharuhen
events.text: Ahmose besieges the Hyksos refuge of Sharuhen in southern Canaan for three years and takes it.

events.title: War against Kush
events.text: Ahmose turns south and campaigns in Nubia against Kerma's allies.

events.title: A new kingdom
events.text: At Abydos, Ahmose's pyramid temple is decorated with some of the earliest scenes of horses and chariots in Egyptian art.

chartNote: Share of the area of modern Egypt, by the power holding each present-day governorate's settled lands. Regions are today's boundaries; the vast desert governorates swing the shares, so the small, rich Delta counts for far less than it did. Frontiers, vassals and every date here are simplified and approximate: chronologies of this period differ by a few decades.
